title: High-performance brain-to-text communication via handwriting
summary: An intracortical brain-computer interface decoded attempted handwriting from motor cortex with a recurrent neural network, letting one participant with spinal cord injury type 90 characters per minute at 94.1% raw online accuracy (above 99% offline with autocorrect).
ai_technology: Recurrent neural network decoder of attempted-handwriting neural activity
organization: Howard Hughes Medical Institute at Stanford University

source_review.scope: Europe PMC metadata and abstract only; Methods not read.

evidence.tested: Single-participant online typing performance reported in abstract.
evidence.unknown: One participant only; generalisation not assessed (abstract only).
evidence.ai_role: RNN decoded attempted handwriting movements into text in real time.
